employers_on_campus.title: Employers On Campus
employers_on_campus.description: Networking opportunities: true when meeting people who can help students' careers is part of this event. That covers employers, companies, firms or industry organizations recruiting, presenting, hosting, co-hosting or sponsoring it (a company named as host or co-host, such as "Ramp x Blueprint" or "Figma x Sanrio", qualifies even for a social); career fairs, employer information sessions and co-op or internship sessions; professionals or alumni sharing their careers or networking with students; career-path panels and advice sessions on breaking into an industry, including ones led by upper-year students; hackathons, designathons, datathons, case competitions and pitch competitions; and professional, industry or academic conferences, symposiums and summits. Online events and events off campus qualify. Ordinary club socials, meetings and workshops with no company, professional or career element, language and gift exchanges, study-abroad, exchange-program and grad school information, wellness, cultural, religious and community-service events, food distributions and performances do not qualify. InteractionBatch.title: InteractionBatch
InteractionBatch.description:
Batch of interactions submitted from a single browser session.

**Trust boundary note on ``user_id``**: this field models the client's
*claim* of which user the batch belongs to.  The server verifies the
claim against the authenticated identity in ``interaction_service._validate_batch``
and 403s on mismatch.  The field is **advisory / diagnostic** -
never trust it for authorization or identity resolution in new code;
use the value resolved from the Bearer token instead.

Typed as ``UUID | None`` so the Pydantic boundary rejects arbitrary
opaque strings (e.g. ``"admin"``) at parse time - if the router-side
ownership check is ever removed during a refactor, impersonation
still cannot succeed because the payload won't even deserialise.
